text:
Claire Nguyen: FYI — Large payments customer asked for a feature we're tentatively calling "Burst Surge Sentinel": very short-lived reservation tokens (15s12m) that increase request success during payment checkout spikes. Key asks: predictable fallback order, a free monthly allowance, and avoid triggering autoscale during flash spikes.
Amit Shah: Sounds like a token-bucket + admission tier. Clarify billing: free allowance (e.g., 250 surge tokens/mo) with per-token overage? Or bill by surge-duration?
Claire Nguyen: Customer prefers free token count (they value predictability). Overages billed per-surge event (flat). They care most about 0% checkout failures within allowed surge tokens.
Lucas Moreno: Engineering sketch: at admission we check tenant surge bucket -> if token available, assign "surge_stamp" and prefer reserved-pool placement. If no token -> run fallback chain: 1) shared reserved lane (best-effort) 2) degrade model (smaller quantized variant) 3) spot capacity 4) 429. Degrade-model fallback is new but could save success rate for checkout flows.
Dana Rodriguez: Important ops constraint: do NOT let surge tokens alone cause autoscale spin-up. Proposed: tag surge traffic in autoscaler as ephemeral with a decay window (120s) and cap its weight to X% of scale trigger. Also provide a tenant-level opt-out to let customers request no-autoscale during pilot.
Amit Shah: Good. For telemetry we need: per-tenant surge tokens remaining, surge accept/fail counts, per-fallback-path counts, and surge-induced latency delta (p95).
Lucas Moreno: Dev breakdown: 1) token service + API + console metrics 2) admission hook + scheduler priority flag 3) fallback implementation for model-degrade path + integration 4) autoscale estimator change (ephemeral weight) 5) simulator & e2e test harness. Rough estimate: 6 infra-weeks + 2 qa-weeks + 2 console-weeks.
Dana Rodriguez: MVP scope suggestion to hit customer pilot in 5 weeks: admission hook + token service + deterministic fallback order + basic console meter + billing event for overage. Skip model-degrade path and autoscale coupling for MVP. That reduces effort to ~3 infra-weeks + 1 console-week.
Claire Nguyen: Acceptance criteria for MVP: 1) surge token admission enforced and visible in Console; 2) synthetic checkout spike test (500 req/s for 60s) for pilot tenant shows <0.3% failures for surge-eligible requests; 3) overage billing event emitted and visible in test invoice; 4) docs + support playbook published.
Amit Shah: Known risks: node-hotspotting if we pack surge requests; billing disputes if customer misunderstands free bucket; support noise. Mitigations: anti-affinity packing, verbose API failure codes ("no_token", "fallback_shared", "fallback_quant"), and pilot SE-managed onboarding.
Lucas Moreno: Ops hooks: emergency global cap per-region, per-tenant disable switch, and auto-detect alert when surge acceptance rate drops below threshold. Also add a low-cost simulator job that runs during canary windows.
Dana Rodriguez: Product decision: name it "Burst Surge Sentinel (soft reserve)" in public docs and avoid using the word "guarantee". For marketing/internal comms use clear SLO language (pilot p95 success target).
ScaleWatchBot: scheduled: run surge-sim on 1788886000 and alert results to #product.
Claire Nguyen: Action items: Lucas -> spike branch feat/burst-sentinel admission prototype by Fri; Amit -> telemetry schema + billing event spec by Thu; Dana -> draft pilot SOW + docs by Tue; I'll update roadmap item and tag legal for billing wording. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
